evidence: In 3d_top, 3d_iso and 3d_iso_back no two component bodies intersect; the passive rows sit close above the screw-terminal bodies but a visible gap remains, though the bottom-left mounting-hole courtyard does encroach on J1's pad area in the 2D view (pad geometry, not a body overlap).
In 3d_iso and 3d_iso_back every screw terminal, the J5 pin header, U1 and all passives sit flush on the PCB surface with no floating, sunken or tilted bodies.
In 3d_top, U1's body is centered between its two pad rows (pin-1 dot aligned), the J5 header covers its four through-holes, and every passive body sits symmetrically between its two end pads.

Screw terminals J1-J4 form a uniform evenly-spaced row on the bottom edge with wire openings facing outward (confirmed in 3d_iso), J5 is a vertical header mating upward, and diodes D1-D4 occupy the identical position/orientation in all four channel strips.

The four ADC channels are identical C-D-R-R strips on a single shared row directly above their respective terminals, and the U1/R9/R10/C1 ADC cluster is tight, so groups read as organized grid-aligned clusters despite large unused board area (a utilization issue, not group scatter).
